t: The Kenya Land and Freedom Army, called the Mau Mau, rose against British colonial rule in Kenya from 1952, after decades of land seizure, forced wage labour and failed petitions; Wangari Maathai names its three issues as land, freedom and self-governance.

The British answered with a State of Emergency, Operation Anvil, a detention system called the Pipeline and the forced resettlement of more than a million Kikuyu in fortified villages; 1,090 people were hanged.
Historians still dispute the death toll, with estimates of 25,000 and 50,000 and a claim of up to 300,000, and whether the conflict was a nationalist rising, an intra-Kikuyu civil war, or both.
dyk: By the end of the Emergency, 1,090 Mau Mau suspects had been executed by hanging, more than double the number executed by the French in Algeria, and at no other time or place in the British Empire was capital punishment dispensed so aggressively.
ev: The Carter Land Commission's report is followed by the seizure of about 7,000,000 acres for the White Highlands
Senior Chief Waruhiu is shot on 9 October and the State of Emergency is declared on 20 October
Mau Mau militants attack Lari on the night of 25 to 26 March, and a retaliatory massacre follows
Operation Anvil clears Nairobi of Kikuyu, Embu and Meru, and villagisation begins in June
Field Marshal Dedan Kimathi is captured on 21 October, ending the British military campaign
Eleven detainees are clubbed to death by guards at the Hola camp
The First Lancaster House Conference sets native Kenyan majority rule in motion
Britain settles with 5,228 claimants for £19.9 million and denies liability

f.where: The British Colony of Kenya: the Kikuyu districts of Central Province, the Aberdares and the forests around Mount Kenya, Nairobi, the Rift Valley and Meru.
f.period: Oathing from about 1943; the State of Emergency declared on 20 October 1952; Operation Anvil (1954); the capture of Dedan Kimathi on 21 October 1956; fighting by Meru units until after independence; an amnesty and army action in 1964 and 1965.
f.figures: Field Marshal Dedan Kimathi; General China; Field Marshal Musa Mwariama; General Baimungi; Field Marshal Muthoni; Jomo Kenyatta, tried as one of the Kapenguria Six; on the British side Governor Evelyn Baring and General George Erskine.
f.outcome: The British campaign ended with Kimathi's capture in 1956 after mass detention, villagisation and 1,090 executions; at least 11,000 deaths among the Mau Mau and other forces, with some estimates considerably higher; Kenyan majority rule was set in motion in January 1960, and independence came in December 1963.
